lessons.title: Discussing contract terms with Google — basics
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar de forma simples sobre os termos básicos de um contrato com o Google — preço, prazo, escopo e responsabilidade — e dizer que prefere tudo por escrito.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a big project, so the contract is very important. The contract has terms: the price, the deadline, the scope, and the responsibility of each side. When the terms are clear, the project is calm. When they are not clear, problems grow. As superintendent of contracts at Racional, this is your daily world.

With a North American client like Google, everything must be fair and in writing. A good partner does not hide things. If something is not clear, you ask to clarify it. If both sides agree, you write it down and you sign. This protects the relationship and the project.

In this lesson you learn the simple English to talk about contract basics. You do not need hard legal words yet. You need short, clear sentences: "This is in the scope", "The price is fixed", "Let us put it in writing". Racional has signed more than 620 projects, and clear terms are always the first step.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para falar de contrato: What is the scope? (qual é o escopo?), Is this included? (isto está incluído?) e Let us put it in writing (vamos colocar por escrito).

Lembre também de We agree on the terms (concordamos com os termos) e This is fair (isto é justo).

lessons.title: "We need to review the contract" — common phrases
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue usar frases simples para pedir tempo e revisar uma proposta do Google com calma, dizendo que vai checar os detalhes e retornar com um retorno.
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, you do not have to answer right away. It is normal and smart to say "we need to review the contract". You take the proposal, you read it carefully, you check the details, and you get back to the client. Asking for time is not weakness. It shows that Racional is serious.

With a big client like Google, the proposal for the data center has many details: price, scope, deadlines, conditions. You want to make sure everything is right before you say yes. So you say "give us a few days" or "I will get back to you by Wednesday". This protects the project and the margin.

In this lesson you learn the polite phrases to slow down and review. You always thank the client first: "we appreciate the offer". Then you ask for time. This is the daily language of a superintendent of contracts, and it keeps the relationship with Google calm and professional.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para pedir tempo com educação: We need to review the proposal (precisamos revisar a proposta), Give us a few days (nos dê alguns dias) e I will get back to you by Wednesday (eu retorno até quarta).

Comece sempre agradecendo: We appreciate the offer (agradecemos a oferta).
lessons.situation: O Google enviou uma proposta para o data center. Você não vai responder na hora — quer revisar com calma e retornar.

lessons.title: Data hall layout — racks, rows, cages
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue descrever, com palavras simples, o layout de um data hall — racks, fileiras, corredores e gaiolas — e dizer onde cada parte fica.
lessons.overview:
The heart of a data center is the data hall. This is the big room with the machines. Inside, the servers sit in tall metal frames called racks. The racks stand in rows, with an aisle between them so people can walk and work. The layout is the plan of all this.

For the Google project, Racional builds this room with care. The floor is often a raised floor, with space under it for cables and cool air. Some clients use a cage to separate their area for extra security. Every rack, row, and aisle has a place. Good layout means easy access and safe work.

In this lesson you learn the simple English to describe a data hall. You can say "the racks are in rows", "the aisle is between the rows", and "the cage is next to the main room". These short sentences help you walk a Google engineer through the space, the same way Racional already does for Microsoft and Amazon.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para descrever o data hall: The racks are in rows (os racks ficam em fileiras), The aisle is between the rows (o corredor fica entre as fileiras) e The cage is next to the main room (a gaiola fica ao lado da sala principal).

Use next to (ao lado de) e between (entre) para dizer onde cada parte fica.

lessons.title: Hosting the Google team at the construction site
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue receber o time do Google na obra com frases simples de boas-vindas e segurança, pedindo que usem os equipamentos de proteção e fiquem juntos durante a visita.
lessons.overview:
When the Google team visits the project, you are the host. A good host makes the visitors feel welcome and, above all, safe. A construction site can be dangerous, so safety first is the rule. You greet the team, you give them the right gear, and you show them around.

Before anyone walks in, everyone must wear a helmet, a vest, and safety glasses. You ask the group to follow you and to stay together at all times. This is normal on every Racional site, and serious clients like Google respect it. Safety shows that the company is professional.

In this lesson you learn warm, simple English to host a client visit. You can say "welcome, glad to have you", "please wear a helmet", and "follow me, please". These short phrases let you host the Google team with confidence and care, the way Racional has done on more than 620 projects.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para receber a visita: Welcome, glad to have you (bem-vindo, é um prazer recebê-lo), Safety first — please wear a helmet (segurança em primeiro lugar — use um capacete) e Please follow me and stay together (por favor, me siga e fiquem juntos).

Use please para soar educado e at all times (o tempo todo) para reforçar a segurança.
lessons.situation: O time do Google chega à obra do data center para uma visita. Você os recebe, entrega os equipamentos de segurança e os guia pelo local.
lessons.context: Welcome to the construction site. We are glad to have you. Safety first, please. Wear a helmet, a vest, and safety glasses. Follow me and stay together at all times.

vocab.example: We host the Google team today.
We are glad to have you.

No helmet, no vest, no problem.
options.whyWrong: Equipamento de segurança é obrigatório na obra.
Numa obra, o time deve ficar junto e seguir o guia.

exercises.title: 3. Ligue o termo à tradução

exercises.title: 4. Escreva suas boas-vindas

exercises.explanation: Tom acolhedor mais segurança clara: é assim que se recebe um cliente na obra.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por cerca de 15 a 20 segundos, receba o time do Google na obra: dê as boas-vindas, peça para usarem capacete, colete e óculos, e diga para seguirem você e ficarem juntos. Use "welcome", "safety first", "helmet" e "follow me".
takeaways: I can welcome a client to the site.
I can say safety first.
I can ask people to wear a helmet and a vest.

I can ask the team to stay together at all times.

teacher.overview: M4 — Coração do programa — negociação comercial com o Google em torno do data center. Cobre defesa de margem, mudança de escopo (change order), force majeure, contract clauses, BATNA, c…

Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Medo de errar trava a fala — valorize a tentativa.

practiceBank.title: Regra crua para frase calorosa

Follow me. → Please follow me this way, and stay together.

practiceBank.title: Fabricio é o visitante do Google

lines: Inverta: O aluno é um visitante do Google chegando à obra e faz perguntas; o professor recebe.
Depois troquem: o aluno recebe usando o vocab de boas-vindas e segurança.

practiceBank.title: Um minuto recebendo o cliente
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala 60s sem parar dando as boas-vindas e instruções de segurança ao time do Google, usando 'welcome', 'safety first', 'to follow me', 'at all times'. Professor conta hesitações.
lines: Dê 60 segundos. Tema: dê as boas-vindas e instruções de segurança ao time do Google.
Exija: 'welcome', 'safety first', 'to follow me', 'at all times'.
Conte as hesitações.

practiceBank.title: Prioridades ao receber o cliente na obra
practiceBank.how: O aluno ordena ações (entregar EPI, dar boas-vindas, explicar rota, pedir para ficarem juntos) por prioridade e justifica oralmente, usando o vocab. Professor questiona se segurança vem antes das boas-vindas.

lessons.title: Introducing the Racional technical team to Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta o time técnico da Racional ao Google em frases curtas, dizendo o nome e a função de cada pessoa para o cliente saber com quem falar.
lessons.overview:
When the Google team comes to the site, the first thing they need is simple: they need to know who is who. A clear introduction of your technical team opens the door for everything else. The client wants to put a name and a face to each role. This is the first step of trust.

At Racional, the team on a data center project is large. There is a project manager, a safety lead, and a site engineer. Each person is responsible for one part of the work. When you say who handles what, the client knows where to go. This saves time on every meeting and every call.

Racional has built more than 620 projects in 50 years, for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and now Google. A strong team is the reason. Today you learn to present that team in English, one person at a time, so Google always has a clear point of contact.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura é simples e muito repetível: "This is [nome]. He is our [função]." Para mulheres, use She is. Para dizer o que a pessoa faz, use "He is responsible for [área]."

Uma frase por pessoa: aponte, fale o nome, fale a função. Sem pressa.
lessons.situation: Primeira reunião técnica na obra do data center. O time do Google chega e você apresenta os engenheiros e o gestor de segurança da Racional, um por um.
lessons.context: Good morning. Let me introduce our team. This is Carlos. He is our project manager. He is responsible for the schedule. This is Ana. She is our safety lead. Please feel free to reach out to them.

vocab.example: She is in charge of quality.
Carlos is your point of contact.

exercises.title: 1. Função e tradução
exercises.explanation: Essas quatro funções aparecem em quase toda reunião de obra com o Google.

exercises.title: 2. Apresente uma pessoa do time
exercises.prompt: Você aponta para o engenheiro de obra e quer dizer o nome e a função dele. A frase mais natural é:

options.text: This is Paulo. He is our site engineer.

options.whyWrong: Faltam os verbos 'is'. A frase precisa de 'is' nos dois lugares.

options.text: He is Paulo site engineer this.
options.whyWrong: A ordem das palavras está embaralhada e não faz sentido.

exercises.title: 3. Complete com a função
exercises.prompt: This is Ana. She is ___ for site safety.
exercises.explanation: 'Responsible for' = responsável por. É a forma mais usada para dizer o que cada pessoa cuida.

exercises.title: 4. Apresente dois colegas
exercises.prompt: Escreva uma apresentação curta de dois membros do seu time para o Google: diga o nome e a função de cada um. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
keywords: responsible for|in charge of|project manager|safety lead|site engineer
exercises.modelAnswer: Let me introduce our team. This is Carlos. He is our project manager. This is Ana. She is responsible for safety.
exercises.explanation: Nome + função, uma frase por pessoa. Simples e claro vale mais que longo.

exercises.title: 5. Apresente o time em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let me introduce our team. This is Carlos. He is our project manager. Please feel free to reach out to him.
exercises.translation: Deixe-me apresentar nossa equipe. Este é o Carlos. Ele é nosso gerente de projeto. Por favor, fique à vontade para procurá-lo.
exercises.prompt: Você está abrindo a reunião na obra. Apresente seu time ao Google, falando alto e com calma.
exercises.explanation: Repita até sair natural. Apontar com a mão enquanto fala ajuda o cliente a acompanhar.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, apresente em inglês uma pessoa real do seu time na Racional para o Google: diga o nome, a função e por que ela é importante no data center.
takeaways: I can introduce my team to Google one person at a time.
I can say a name and a role with 'This is... He is our...'.
I can use 'responsible for' to explain each role.
I can tell Google who their point of contact is.

teacher.overview: M4 — Coração do programa — negociação comercial com o Google em torno do data center. Cobre defesa de margem, mudança de escopo (change order), force majeure, contract clauses, BATNA, c…
teacher.focus: Relacionamento e cortesia; abrir e conduzir a conversa.

flow.how: Aluno reconta em inglês, em 60s, o que praticou na aula anterior.
Frase-base fixa; troque um elemento por vez (cliente, prazo, valor), oralmente.
Professor e aluno têm, cada um, metade da informação e se perguntam para completar.
Aplique o alvo a uma situação real do projeto do aluno.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Medo de errar trava a fala — valorize a tentativa.
Equilibrar formal × casual conforme o interlocutor.

practiceBank.title: Apresentando o time na chegada do Google
practiceBank.how: Em duplas, o aluno recebe o time do Google na portaria da obra do data center e apresenta 3 pessoas da Racional, uma por uma ('This is Ana, our site engineer; she is in charge of...'). O professor faz o papel do cliente e pergunta 'who should I reach out to about X?'. Aluno PRODUZ usando 'to introduce', 'responsible for', 'your point of contact'.
lines: Set the scene: 'You are at the gate of the Google data center site. Fabricio, the Google team just arrived — introduce three of your people, one by one.'
Prompt the start: 'Begin with: This is Ana, our site engineer; she is in charge of...'
Fire as the client: 'Nice to meet you. Who should I reach out to about the power room?'
Fire as the client: 'And who is responsible for safety on this site?'
Fire as the client: 'If I have a question about the schedule, who is my point of contact?'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Quem faz o quê no organograma
practiceBank.how: Professor entrega ao aluno um organograma com nomes mas sem funções; o aluno tem as funções numa lista separada. Ele liga cada pessoa ao seu papel falando 'Carlos handles safety, he is the safety lead'. Pratica 'role', 'to handle', 'project manager', 'to report to'.
lines: Hand over the org chart: 'Here are the names; here is your list of roles. Match each person out loud.'
Model the target: 'Say it like this — Carlos handles safety, he is the safety lead.'
Prompt: 'Now do the project manager — who is it and who do they report to?'
Push: 'Good. Who does the site engineer report to?'
Require: 'Use to handle and to report to in every answer.'

practiceBank.title: Mini-vídeo de apresentação do time
practiceBank.how: Aluno grava 60 segundos no celular apresentando o time técnico da Racional como se fosse abrir uma reunião com o Google. Deve nomear pelo menos 4 papéis e dizer a quem cada um reporta. Professor ouve depois e corrige uso de 'in charge of' e 'reach out'.
lines: Dictate the task: 'Record 60 seconds on your phone opening a meeting with Google. Name at least four roles and say who each one reports to.'
Require these words: 'in charge of', 'reach out', 'your point of contact', 'responsible for'.
Start them: 'Open with: Good morning, let me introduce the Racional technical team.'
After listening, follow up: 'You said in charge of for two people — who is in charge of the schedule exactly?'

practiceBank.title: Com quem eu falo sobre isso?
practiceBank.how: Professor dispara perguntas rápidas do tipo cliente ('Who do I call about the power room?', 'Who handles the schedule?') e o aluno responde na hora indicando a pessoa e o papel. Foco em respostas curtas com 'your point of contact is...', 'feel free to reach out to...'.
lines: Ping-pong, rapid fire: 'Who do I call about the power room?'
'Who handles the schedule?'
'Who do I report a safety issue to?'
'Who is responsible for the structure?'
'Who is my main point of contact on site?'
'Who should I talk to about the data hall handover?'

practiceBank.title: Eu sou o gestor do projeto
practiceBank.how: Aluno senta na cadeira quente como project manager da Racional e os colegas/professor perguntam sobre os papéis do time. Ele responde apresentando cada colleague e o que cada um faz no data center. Usa 'colleague', 'role', 'responsible for'.
lines: Set the hot seat: 'Fabricio, you are the project manager of the Racional data center. We will ask you about your team.'
Ask: 'What is your role on this project?'
Ask: 'Who is your safety lead and what is he responsible for?'
Ask: 'Tell me about your colleague who runs the structure work.'
Require: 'Use colleague, role and responsible for in your answers.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Descrevendo o crachá do time
practiceBank.how: Professor mostra 4 crachás com foto, nome e cargo. O aluno descreve oralmente cada pessoa e sua função para o Google ('She is our safety lead, in charge of all site safety'). Pratica vocabulário de cargos e 'in charge of'.
lines: Show the badges: 'I'm holding four badges — photo, name, title. Describe each person and their role to Google.'
Model: 'Like this — She is our safety lead, in charge of all site safety.'
Prompt the next badge: 'Now the project manager — describe him.'
Push: 'Use in charge of for at least three of the four.'

practiceBank.title: O aluno vira cliente do Google
practiceBank.how: Aluno assume o papel do engenheiro do Google e o professor apresenta o time da Racional com erros propositais. O aluno-cliente pede esclarecimentos ('So who do I report a safety issue to?'), forçando-o a processar 'safety lead', 'to report to', 'point of contact'.
lines: Flip roles: 'Now you are the Google engineer. I will introduce the Racional team — but I will make mistakes.'
Plant an error: 'This is Ana, she is responsible for the schedule and also the safety lead.'
Force the clarifying question: 'So who do I report a safety issue to?'
Plant another error: 'Carlos handles everything on site.'
Prompt: 'Ask me who your real point of contact is.'

practiceBank.title: Encontre o responsável
practiceBank.how: Com cartões de papéis distribuídos, o aluno circula perguntando 'Are you in charge of the schedule?' até montar o time completo da obra. Cada acerto exige a frase 'You are the project manager, responsible for...'. Pratica 'responsible for', 'in charge of', 'role'.
lines: Mingle setup: 'You have role cards. Circle the room asking until you find each person of the data center team.'
Model the question: 'Ask like this — Are you in charge of the schedule?'
Require the confirmation line: 'When you find them, say: You are the project manager, responsible for...'
Push: 'Use responsible for, in charge of and role on every match.'

practiceBank.title: Abertura da primeira reunião técnica

lessons.title: Talking about budget — "we are within budget"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você confirma ao Google que o projeto está dentro do orçamento, dizendo "we are within budget" e dando um número simples para sustentar a afirmação.
lessons.overview:
In any project, money is a key topic. The Google team wants to know one thing fast: is the data center within budget? When you can say "yes" in clear English, you give the client calm and trust. Good news about cost is good news for everyone.

A project is on track when the work and the money go as planned. To be under budget is even better: it means you spend less than the forecast. At Racional, cost control is part of the culture. The team reports the numbers every phase, so there are no surprises for the client.

Racional has delivered more than 10 million square meters of work in 50 years. Strong budget control is one big reason clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google come back. Today you learn the simple words to report good cost news with confidence.
lessons.intro:
A frase que tranquiliza o cliente é "We are within budget." — estamos dentro do orçamento. Para dar o número, use "We are two percent under budget." (2% abaixo, ótima notícia).

Note: within = dentro de; under = abaixo de. Afirme primeiro, depois dê o número.
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal de acompanhamento com o time financeiro do Google. Eles perguntam como está o custo do data center. Você confirma que está tudo dentro do previsto.
lessons.context: Thank you for the question. I am glad to report good news. We are within budget. In fact, we are two percent under the forecast. Costs are under control. We are on track for this phase.

vocab.example: We are two percent under budget.
The cost is low this phase.
I report the numbers every month.
I'm glad to report good news.
So far, we are on track.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: We are within budget.
exercises.explanation: 'Within budget' = dentro do orçamento. É a frase que tranquiliza o cliente.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a frase

exercises.title: 3. Complete com a palavra certa
exercises.prompt: Costs are ___ control. We are on track.
exercises.explanation: 'Under control' = sob controle. É uma frase curta que passa segurança ao Google.

exercises.title: 4. Dê a boa notícia
exercises.prompt: O Google pergunta sobre o custo e você quer dizer que está tudo dentro do previsto. A melhor frase é:

options.text: Budget is bad and we no track.
options.whyWrong: A frase está incorreta e passa a mensagem errada.

options.text: I am glad to report we are within budget.
We within the over budget forecast.
options.whyWrong: As palavras estão fora de ordem e não fazem sentido.

exercises.title: 5. Reporte em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I am glad to report we are within budget. We are two percent under the forecast.
exercises.translation: Tenho o prazer de informar que estamos dentro do orçamento. Estamos dois por cento abaixo da previsão.

exercises.explanation: Afirme primeiro, depois dê o número. Fale devagar para o cliente ouvir bem.

takeaways: I can say 'We are within budget.' with confidence.
I can give a simple number like 'two percent under budget'.
I can say 'Costs are under control.'
I can report good news to Google in clear English.

practiceBank.how: Simula-se o follow-up mensal com o financeiro do Google. O aluno abre com 'I'm glad to report we are within budget' e sustenta com um número simples. Professor faz perguntas de acompanhamento ('and the next phase?'). Pratica 'within budget', 'on track', 'forecast', 'as planned'.

practiceBank.title: Como está o custo?
practiceBank.how: Professor faz perguntas rápidas de cliente sobre custo do data center e o aluno responde sempre tranquilizando com números simples ('Spending is under control, we are under budget by 2%'). Foco em respostas curtas com 'under control', 'so far', 'on track'.

'Are we still on track?'
'Are we over or under budget right now?'
'How is spending so far?'
'And the forecast for next month?'
'Any surprises in the costs?'

practiceBank.title: Update de orçamento em 60 segundos
practiceBank.how: Aluno grava um update falado de 1 minuto confirmando ao Google que o projeto está dentro do orçamento, citando uma fase e um número. Deve usar 'I'm glad to report', 'forecast' e 'as planned'. Professor revê e corrige depois.
lines: Dictate the task: 'Record a 60-second budget update for Google. Name one phase and give one number.'
Require these words: 'I'm glad to report', 'forecast', 'as planned', 'within budget'.
Start them: 'Open with: I'm glad to report the data center is within budget.'
After listening, follow up: 'You said as planned — which phase exactly is as planned?'

practiceBank.title: Completando o relatório de custos
practiceBank.how: Aluno A tem os custos previstos e B tem os reais; trocando informação oralmente, descobrem se o data center está within budget. Conversam usando 'forecast', 'spending', 'within budget', 'approved'.
lines: Set the information gap: 'You have the forecast costs; I have the actual costs. Talk it through to find out if the data center is within budget.'
Model: 'Ask like this — what was the actual spending on the structure phase?'
Require: 'Use forecast, spending, within budget and approved as you compare.'
Push to a conclusion: 'So — are we within budget or not? Say it in one line.'

practiceBank.title: Tranquilizando o CFO do Google
practiceBank.how: Professor faz um CFO nervoso que teme estouro de custo. O aluno o acalma com fatos e frases positivas ('We are on track, spending is as planned, so far so good'). Produção de linguagem reassegurante com o vocabulário da aula.
lines: Set the role-play: 'I am a nervous CFO at Google. I'm worried we'll blow the budget. Calm me down with facts.'
Press: 'I heard material costs are rising — are we still okay?'
Press: 'How can you be so sure spending stays under control?'
Force reassurance: 'Use We are on track, spending is as planned, so far so good.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Lendo o gráfico de orçamento
practiceBank.how: Professor mostra um gráfico simples de orçamento previsto vs gasto. O aluno descreve para o Google que está dentro do previsto ('Spending is below the forecast, we are within budget'). Pratica 'cost', 'forecast', 'spending', 'phase'.
lines: Show the chart: 'Here is a simple budget chart — forecast versus actual spending. Describe it to Google.'
Model: 'Like this — Spending is below the forecast, so we are within budget.'
Prompt: 'Which phase shows the biggest gap below forecast?'
Require: 'Use cost, forecast, spending and phase.'

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sobre o status financeiro
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala 60 segundos sem parar sobre o status de custo do data center, sem hesitações longas. Deve encaixar 'within budget', 'on track', 'as planned' e um número. Professor marca pausas longas.
lines: Just a minute: 'Talk for 60 seconds, no long pauses, on the financial status of the data center.'
Require these words: 'within budget', 'on track', 'as planned', plus one number.
Start them: 'Begin with: So far, the data center is fully within budget.'
Note: 'Marco cada pausa longa; depois você refaz mais fluente.'

practiceBank.title: Status por fase
practiceBank.how: Aluno entrevista o professor (que tem dados por fase) perguntando o custo de cada fase do data center e depois faz o report back ao 'Google': 'All phases are on track and within budget'. Usa 'phase', 'approved', 'forecast'.
lines: Survey setup: 'I have the cost data per phase. Interview me phase by phase, then report back to Google.'
Model the question: 'Ask like this — what is the cost status of the MEP phase?'
Require the report-back line: 'Close with: All phases are on track and within budget.'
Push: 'Use phase, approved and forecast.'

practiceBank.title: Número cru vira boa notícia
practiceBank.how: Professor dá um número ('5% below plan'); o aluno transforma numa frase de reporte positivo ('Great news — we are 5% under budget, as planned'). Rodadas rápidas reforçando 'under budget', 'within budget', 'on track'.
lines: Drill, I give a raw number, you turn it into good news: '5% below plan' → 'Great news — we are 5% under budget, as planned.'
'2% under forecast' → 'I'm glad to report we are 2% within budget, right on track.'
'spending flat this month' → 'Spending is under control this month, fully as planned.'

practiceBank.title: Onde economizamos mais
practiceBank.how: Dadas 4 fases do data center com economias diferentes, o aluno ordena da mais à menos econômica e justifica oralmente ao Google por que cada uma ficou within budget. Usa 'spending', 'forecast', 'approved'.
lines: Set the ranking: 'Here are four data center phases with different savings. Rank them from most to least economical and justify each to Google.'
Model: 'Like this — The structure phase saved the most because spending stayed below forecast.'
Push: 'Why did the MEP phase still end up within budget?'
Require: 'Use spending, forecast and approved in every justification.'

practiceBank.title: Liberar verba da próxima fase
practiceBank.how: Em 4 minutos, o aluno convence o financeiro do Google a aprovar a verba da próxima fase mostrando que tudo até aqui ficou within budget. Professor resiste pedindo números. Pratica 'approved', 'forecast', 'as planned', 'on track'.
lines: Timed negotiation: 'You have 4 minutes to convince Google's finance team to approve the next phase budget.'
Start them: 'Open with: Everything so far is within budget, so I'd like to request approval for the next phase.'
Resist as client: 'Show me the numbers — why should I approve this now?'
Resist again: 'What does your forecast say for this next phase?'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Ligação rápida de status de custo
practiceBank.how: Costas com costas, o aluno liga para o Google e dá, só de ouvido, a confirmação de que o data center está dentro do orçamento. O cliente confirma o número repetindo. Força clareza com 'within budget', 'so far', 'I'm glad to report'.
lines: Back-to-back phone setup: 'No video. Call Google and confirm, by voice only, that the data center is within budget.'
Start them: 'Open with: Quick status call — I'm glad to report we're within budget.'
As client, repeat to confirm: 'So you're saying we're two percent under, correct?'
Push: 'Make it clear with within budget, so far and I'm glad to report.'

lessons.title: Over budget conversation — "we are 3% over"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você comunica ao Google, de forma transparente e calma, que o projeto está acima do orçamento, dizendo "we are three percent over" e oferecendo um plano.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the news is not perfect. The project can go over budget. This is normal in big construction. What the Google team values most is honesty. To be transparent early is much better than to hide a problem. A small number shared on time builds trust.

When costs go up, there is always a reason: a change in scope, higher material costs, or a new request. Your job is to explain the reason in simple words and to share a plan to recover. At Racional, the rule is to keep the client informed at every step.

For 50 years, Racional has worked with demanding clients like Microsoft and Amazon. Honest communication is why these partnerships last. Today you learn to give difficult cost news to Google in a calm and clear way.
lessons.intro:
Quando o custo sobe, a chave é a transparência: "To be honest, we are three percent over budget." Diga o número, depois a causa (due to a change in scope) e ofereça um plano.

Use frases curtas: "There is a reason." + "We have a plan." + "I will keep you informed."
lessons.situation: Reunião com o time financeiro do Google. Houve uma mudança de escopo no data center e o custo subiu. Você precisa ser honesto e mostrar controle.
lessons.context: I want to be transparent with you. We are three percent over budget. This is due to a change in scope. Material costs went up. We have a plan to recover. I will keep you informed.

vocab.example: We are three percent over budget.
This is due to a change.
There was a change in scope.
We have a plan to recover.

exercises.explanation: Número primeiro, depois a causa, depois o plano. Honestidade gera confiança.

practiceBank.title: Reunião difícil: estamos 3% acima
practiceBank.how: Aluno comunica ao financeiro do Google, calmo e transparente, que o data center está 3% acima do orçamento por mudança de escopo, e oferece um plano. Professor reage com pressão. Pratica 'over budget', 'due to', 'change in scope', 'a plan', 'to recover'.

practiceBank.title: Plano para recuperar o overrun
practiceBank.how: Diante de um estouro de 3% causado por alta de materiais, o aluno propõe oralmente um plano de 3 passos para recuperar custo no data center. Professor questiona cada passo. Usa 'overrun', 'material costs', 'to recover', 'the reason'.

Question: 'What is the reason this plan will work?'
Require: 'Use overrun, material costs, to recover and the reason.'

practiceBank.title: Comunicado honesto de estouro
practiceBank.how: Aluno grava 60s comunicando ao Google, de forma honesta, que estão over budget, explicando o porquê e prometendo manter informado. Deve usar 'to be transparent', 'honest', 'to keep you informed', 'due to'. Professor revê depois.
lines: Dictate the task: 'Record 60 seconds telling Google, honestly, that you are over budget — explain why and promise to keep them informed.'
Require these words: 'to be transparent', 'honest', 'to keep you informed', 'due to'.
Start them: 'Open with: To be transparent and honest, we are currently over budget.'
After listening, follow up: 'You said due to — due to what, exactly?'

practiceBank.title: Cliente cético sobre o custo extra
practiceBank.how: Professor faz um cliente do Google que duvida da justificativa do estouro ('Why should we accept this 3%?'). O aluno defende com transparência e o plano de recuperação. Produção argumentativa com 'change in scope', 'material costs', 'to explain'.
lines: Set the devil's advocate: 'I'm a skeptical Google client who doubts your reason for the overrun.'
Challenge: 'Why should we accept this 3%? Sounds like poor planning.'
Challenge: 'A change in scope? That sounds like your problem, not ours.'
Force a defense: 'Explain the material costs and the change in scope clearly.'
Require: 'Use change in scope, material costs and to explain.'

practiceBank.title: Notícia ruim dita com calma
practiceBank.how: Professor dá uma frase seca ('Costs went up 3%'); o aluno reformula com tato e plano ('I want to be transparent: we are three percent over, due to a change in scope, and here is our plan'). Rodadas rápidas.
lines: Drill, I give a blunt line, you soften it with tact and a plan: 'Costs went up 3%' → 'I want to be transparent: we are three percent over, due to a change in scope, and here is our plan.'
'Materials got expensive' → 'To be honest, material costs went up, which is the reason we're slightly over — and we have a plan to recover.'
'We're over budget' → 'I'll be straight with you: we are three percent over budget, and I'd like to share the recovery plan.'

Interrupt: 'And how do I know this won't grow?'

practiceBank.title: Rastreando a causa do estouro

Model: 'Ask like this — which materials went up, and by how much?'
Require: 'Use material costs, to go up, change in scope and the reason.'

practiceBank.title: Respondendo o e-mail do Google sobre custo
practiceBank.how: Professor lê um e-mail do Google preocupado com o aumento. O aluno responde oralmente, como numa ligação, sendo honesto sobre o overrun e oferecendo o plano. Pratica 'to be transparent', 'to share details', 'to recover'.
lines: Read the email aloud: 'Hi, we're concerned costs are rising on the data center. Can you explain?'
Prompt the spoken reply: 'Answer as if on a call — be honest about the overrun and offer the plan.'
Start them: 'Open with: Thanks for flagging this — let me be transparent with you.'
Require: 'Use to be transparent, to share details and to recover.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Na berlinda pelo overrun
practiceBank.how: Aluno na cadeira quente como gestor do projeto; colegas/professor disparam perguntas duras sobre o 3% acima. Ele responde mantendo a calma e a transparência. Foco em 'honest', 'due to', 'to keep you informed'.

lessons.title: UPS — uninterruptible power supply for Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao Google, com vocabulário técnico simples, o que é o UPS de um data center e por que ele garante energia sem interrupção para os servidores.
lessons.overview:
A data center can never stop. The servers must run all day and all night. This is why the UPS, the uninterruptible power supply, is one of the most important systems. For Google, uptime is everything. The UPS protects it.

The idea is simple. If there is a power outage, the UPS uses battery backup and switches over instantly. It keeps the servers running until the generator takes over. The system is redundant and reliable, so the data center never goes dark.

At Racional, power systems are a core part of every data center we build for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. When you can explain the UPS in clear English, you show the client that the team knows the technical work. Today you learn the key words to do exactly that.
lessons.intro:
A ideia central: se a energia da rede cai (a power outage), o UPS entra instantly com energia de bateria (battery backup) até o gerador assumir.

A frase-âncora é simples: "The UPS keeps the servers running." Explique a função primeiro, o detalhe técnico depois.
lessons.situation: Visita técnica ao data center. Um engenheiro do Google aponta para a sala de energia e pergunta como você garante que os servidores nunca desligam.
lessons.context: This is our UPS, the power supply. If there is a power outage, the UPS switches over instantly. It uses battery backup. It keeps the servers running. Then the generator takes over. The system is reliable.

lessons.title: Reading the room — when to speak, when to listen
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você percebe a hora certa de falar e a hora de ouvir numa reunião com o Google, usando frases curtas para mostrar que acompanha e para entrar no momento certo.
lessons.overview:
In a meeting, when you speak is as important as what you say. To read the room means to feel the right moment. Sometimes you talk. Sometimes you listen. The Google team values a partner who knows the difference. This is a quiet skill, but a strong one.

When you listen well, you can use small phrases to show it: "I see.", "That makes sense.", "Please go on." When you want to add a point, you wait for the right moment and then you jump in with care. A short pause is your friend. It shows respect and control.

At Racional, meetings with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google are about trust, not only about facts. A leader who listens first earns the room. Today you learn the simple English to show you are present and to speak at the right time.
lessons.intro:
Para mostrar que você acompanha, use frases curtas: "I see.", "That makes sense.", "Please go on."

Para entrar na conversa na hora certa, use "If I may add..." ou "May I share a thought?". Espere a pausa, depois fale.
lessons.situation: Reunião de alinhamento com o Google. O cliente fala bastante. Você precisa mostrar que está acompanhando e entrar com seu ponto no momento certo.
lessons.context: I see. That makes sense. Please go on. I am listening. If I may add one thought: we can start next week. Thank you. Please continue.

vocab.example: A good leader can read the room.

practiceBank.title: O cliente fala muito, eu acompanho

practiceBank.title: Entrar com o ponto certo na hora certa
practiceBank.how: O cliente do Google explica um problema longo; o aluno deve identificar a pausa e entrar com uma solução breve usando 'if I may add' ou 'to share a thought'. Professor avalia o timing. Usa 'a pause', 'to jump in', 'your view'.

Explain long: 'The cooling alarms keep going off at night, and we don't know if it's the sensors or the load...'
Leave a pause: '...so we're stuck.'
Evaluate: 'Did you wait for the pause? Use a pause, to jump in, your view.'

practiceBank.title: Interromper vira acompanhar
practiceBank.how: Professor dá uma frase que corta o cliente; o aluno reformula como sinal de escuta + entrada educada ('I see — and if I may add...'). Rodadas reforçando 'that makes sense', 'please go on', 'if I may add'.
lines: Drill, I give an interrupting line, you reshape it as listening + a polite entry: '(cuts in) No, that's wrong.' → 'I see — and if I may add, here's another angle.'
'(cuts in) Let me stop you there.' → 'That makes sense — please go on, and then I'd like to share a thought.'
'(cuts in) Actually, no.' → 'I see your point — if I may add one thing when you're done.'

practiceBank.title: Na berlinda como ouvinte
practiceBank.how: Aluno na cadeira quente deve responder a uma rajada de fala do professor usando só sinais de escuta no momento certo e uma única entrada de conteúdo. Treina 'I'm listening', 'go ahead', 'to share a thought'.
lines: Set the hot seat: 'I'll fire a burst of talk at you. Respond only with listening signals at the right time, plus one single content point.'
Burst: 'Schedule, budget, safety, the handover — it's all moving at once and I need to get through it...'
Leave a gap: '...okay, your thoughts?'
Require: 'Use I'm listening, go ahead, to share a thought.'

lessons.title: Polite interruption — "May I add something?"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você interrompe com educação numa reunião com o Google, pedindo licença para acrescentar um ponto de forma breve e respeitosa.
lessons.overview:
In every meeting, there is a moment when you need to speak before the other person ends. This is an interruption. Done well, it is polite and useful. Done badly, it feels rude. With Google, the right words make all the difference. A short, kind phrase opens the door.

The key is to ask first and to be brief. You can say "May I add something?" or "Sorry to interrupt, just a quick point." You make your point in a few words, and then you let the client continue. "I'll be quick" shows respect for their time.

At Racional, leaders in meetings with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google know that how you interrupt shapes the relationship. A polite point can save time and add value. Today you learn the simple English to interrupt with care and still be heard.
lessons.intro:
A frase-âncora é educada e curta: "May I add something?" ou "Sorry to interrupt — just a quick point."

Peça licença, fale breve, devolva a palavra: "I'll be quick." + "Please continue."
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google. O cliente está explicando e você percebe um ponto importante que precisa entrar agora, sem ser rude.

lessons.title: Talking about milestones — "we hit milestone 3"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reporta o progresso do data center ao Google por marcos, dizendo "We hit milestone three" e apontando o próximo passo. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Big projects move forward in milestones. A milestone is a key delivery point. At the Google data center, the Racional team reaches one milestone, and then the next. The client wants to see where the project is today and what comes next.

In a monthly status meeting, you report each milestone. You say what is complete and what is on track. You also say if the work is on schedule or ahead of schedule. Clear reports build trust. Google sees that Racional controls the timeline.

Racional knows this well. In more than fifty years and over 620 projects, the company delivers by milestones. For a global client like Google, simple and honest progress reports are very important. Good English here means good control of the schedule.
lessons.intro:
A frase-âncora é "We hit milestone three." — atingimos o marco 3. Use to hit a milestone = alcançar um marco.

Depois aponte o próximo: "We are on track for milestone four." (no caminho para o marco 4) e diga o ritmo: "on schedule" (no prazo) ou "ahead of schedule" (adiantado).
lessons.situation: Reunião de status mensal com o Google. Eles querem saber o progresso do data center. Você reporta o marco atingido e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.context: Good news on progress. We hit milestone three last week. The main structure is complete, right on schedule. Now we are on track for milestone four. Next up is the data hall, by the end of next month.

vocab.example: We hit milestone three last week.

options.text: We miss milestone three on schedule.
options.whyWrong: 'Miss' é PERDER o marco. Se você o alcançou, o verbo é 'hit' ou 'reach'.

Prompt: 'Which milestones have we already reached?'
Push: 'What's next up after this one?'
Require: 'Use milestone, to reach and to hit a milestone.'

practiceBank.title: Perguntas rápidas do Google
practiceBank.how: Professor dispara perguntas curtas ('Are you on schedule?', 'Did you hit milestone two?', 'What's next?'). Aluno responde em uma frase usando o vocab do marco. Troquem de lado: aluno faz as perguntas e professor responde com erros para o aluno corrigir.
lines: Ping-pong, rapid fire, one-sentence answers: 'Are you on schedule?'
'Did you hit milestone two?'
'What's next up?'
'Are you ahead or behind schedule?'
'Are you on track for the data hall?'
Then swap: 'Now you ask me — I'll answer with errors for you to correct.'

practiceBank.title: Reunião de status com 3 marcos
practiceBank.how: Simulem uma reunião onde o aluno apresenta 3 marcos seguidos: um 'on schedule', um 'ahead of schedule', um 'behind schedule'. Aluno deve justificar cada status e indicar o 'next step'. Professor anota e cobra o vocab que faltar.
lines: Open the simulation: 'Present three milestones in a row — one on schedule, one ahead of schedule, one behind schedule. Justify each and give the next step.'
Start them: 'Begin with: Milestone one is on schedule.'
Prompt: 'Now the one that's ahead — explain why.'
Prompt: 'And the one behind — what's the next step?'
Require: 'Use on schedule, ahead of schedule, behind schedule, next step.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Trocando o status do marco
practiceBank.how: Professor dá uma frase ('Milestone three is on schedule') e pede para o aluno reformular para 'ahead of schedule', 'behind schedule' e 'on track for next week'. Aluno produz cada variação em voz alta, mantendo sentido técnico do data center.
lines: Drill, I give a status, you reformulate it three ways: 'Milestone three is on schedule' → 'ahead of schedule' → 'behind schedule' → 'on track for next week'.
'Milestone four is on schedule' → 'ahead of schedule' / 'behind schedule' / 'on track for the end of the month'.
'The data hall milestone is on schedule' → 'ahead of schedule' / 'behind schedule' / 'on track for next quarter'.

practiceBank.title: A história do marco que adiantamos
practiceBank.how: Aluno conta uma mini-história: como a equipe 'hit a milestone ahead of schedule' no data center do Google. Deve usar pelo menos 6 termos do vocab e terminar com 'next up'. Professor escuta sem interromper e dá feedback no fim.
lines: Set the storytelling: 'Tell a mini-story — how the team hit a milestone ahead of schedule at Google's data center. Use at least six vocab terms and end with next up.'
Start them: 'Begin with: Last month, we hit a milestone ahead of schedule.'
Require: 'milestone, to reach, on schedule, deliverable, progress, next up.'
After, give feedback at the end — no interruptions during.

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sobre os deliverables
practiceBank.how: Aluno fala 60 segundos sem parar sobre os 'deliverables' do mês, sem hesitar muito nem repetir. Tem que usar 'deliverable', 'to complete', 'deadline', 'by the end of'. Professor cronometra e marca pausas longas.
lines: Just a minute: 'Talk for 60 seconds, no stopping, about this month's deliverables.'
Require these words: 'deliverable', 'to complete', 'deadline', 'by the end of'.
Start them: 'Begin with: This month we have three key deliverables.'
Note: 'Cronometro e marco as pausas longas.'

practiceBank.title: Defendendo o cronograma na cadeira quente
practiceBank.how: Aluno senta na 'cadeira quente' como responsável pelo data center; professor e (se houver) colegas disparam perguntas sobre prazos e marcos. Aluno responde tudo na hora usando 'to meet a deadline', 'on track for', 'on schedule'.
lines: Set the hot seat: 'You're the data center lead. We fire questions about deadlines and milestones — answer all on the spot.'
Ask: 'Will you meet the deadline for the data hall?'
Ask: 'Are you on track for milestone five?'
Ask: 'Which milestone are you on right now?'
Require: 'Use to meet a deadline, on track for and on schedule.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Pesquisa de status entre frentes
practiceBank.how: Aluno entrevista o professor (que faz 3 papéis: civil, elétrica, MEP) sobre o status de cada frente, anota e depois reporta ao 'Google' consolidando: quem está on/ahead/behind schedule e o 'next up' de cada um.
lines: Survey setup: 'I'll play three fronts — civil, electrical, MEP. Interview me on each one's status, then report back to Google.'
Model the question: 'Ask like this — is the electrical front on schedule?'
Require the report-back: 'Consolidate — who is on, ahead, or behind, and the next up for each.'
Push: 'Use on schedule, ahead of schedule, next up.'

practiceBank.title: PT → EN dos marcos
practiceBank.how: Professor diz frases curtas em PT ('Atingimos o marco três', 'Estamos adiantados', 'O próximo passo é liberar o data hall'). Aluno traduz na hora para inglês usando o vocab estudado. Ritmo rápido, foco em automatizar 'to hit a milestone' e 'next up'.
lines: Lightning translation, PT to EN, rapid: 'Atingimos o marco três.' → 'We hit milestone three.'
'Estamos adiantados.' → 'We are ahead of schedule.'
'O próximo passo é liberar o data hall.' → 'Next up is to release the data hall.'
Coach: 'Ritmo rápido — automatize to hit a milestone e next up.'

practiceBank.title: Pitch de 30s do progresso ao diretor do Google
practiceBank.how: Aluno encontra o diretor do Google no elevador e tem 30s para resumir onde o data center está: marco atual, se está no prazo e o próximo entregável. Deve soar confiante. Professor cronometra e pede uma 2ª versão mais enxuta.
lines: Elevator pitch: 'You meet Google's director in the elevator — 30 seconds to summarize where the data center is: current milestone, schedule, next deliverable.'
Start them: 'Open with: Quick update — we just hit milestone three, on schedule.'
Require: 'Use milestone, on schedule, deliverable, next up.'
Follow up: 'Now a tighter, leaner second version.'

leadIn: Which milestone is the data center on right now?
Are you on schedule, ahead of schedule, or behind schedule this month?
What is the next milestone, or 'next up', for the data hall?
What's one deliverable you have to complete by the end of the month?
How does Google usually like to hear about progress — by milestones or by dates?

pill.tip: Algumas siglas se soletram, não se leem como palavra: "CEO" é 'si-i-ÔU' e "KPI" é "kêi-pi-ÁI". A última letra costuma levar a força.
pill.sample: The CEO asked for the new KPI before the call.

lessons.title: Missed milestone conversation with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz com calma a conversa com o Google quando um marco não foi cumprido — reconhece o fato, dá o motivo curto e mostra o plano de recuperação. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a milestone is late. The work slips, and a delivery date is not met. This is hard, but it happens in big projects. With Google, the best way is not to hide it. The best way is to be honest and clear.

The talk has three simple steps. First, you acknowledge the fact: we missed the milestone. Second, you give the reason in one short line. Third, you show the recovery plan: how Racional brings the work back on track. You take responsibility, and then you point to the solution.

For Racional, trust is the base of every client relationship. In over 620 projects, the company learned one thing: a client respects an honest report more than a perfect excuse. With Google, owning the problem and fixing it keeps the partnership strong.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura é em três passos: acknowledge (reconheça), explain (motivo curto) e recover (mostre o plano).

Frases-âncora: "We missed the milestone.", "The reason was a late delivery." e "Here is our recovery plan." Use o passado para o fato e o futuro (will) para a solução.
lessons.situation: Reunião de acompanhamento com o Google. O marco de liberação do data hall não foi atingido na data combinada. Você abre a conversa de frente, com tom firme e calmo.
lessons.context: I want to be straight with you. We missed the data hall milestone. The reason was a late equipment delivery. We take responsibility for this. Here is our recovery plan to bring the schedule back on track next month.

vocab.example: We missed the data hall milestone.
I want to be straight with you.
The reason was a late delivery.
The date slipped by two weeks.
We will bring the schedule back on track.
We commit to the new date.
Going forward, we will report weekly.
I will be honest with you.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: We missed the milestone. Here is our recovery plan.
exercises.explanation: Reconheça o fato e aponte logo o plano. É o coração da conversa difícil.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a frase do motivo
exercises.explanation: 'The reason was a late delivery.' — motivo curto e direto, em uma frase só.

exercises.title: 3. Assuma a responsabilidade
exercises.prompt: We take ___ for this delay.
exercises.explanation: 'To take responsibility' = assumir a responsabilidade. Mostra controle, não desculpa.

exercises.title: 4. Abra a conversa difícil
exercises.prompt: O marco atrasou. Como você abre a conversa com o Google?

options.text: I want to be straight with you. We missed the milestone.
It is not our problem. The milestone is fine.
options.whyWrong: Esconder o fato quebra a confiança. Reconheça o atraso de frente.

options.text: Maybe we miss something, I am not sure.
options.whyWrong: Vago demais. Seja claro: 'We missed the milestone.'

exercises.title: 5. Conduza a conversa em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We missed the milestone. The reason was a late delivery. Here is our recovery plan.
exercises.translation: Perdemos o marco. O motivo foi uma entrega atrasada. Aqui está o nosso plano de recuperação.
exercises.prompt: Abra a conversa com o Google em três passos: reconheça, explique o motivo e aponte o plano.
exercises.explanation: Reconhecer, explicar, recuperar. Nunca pare na má notícia: termine no plano.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, imagine que o data hall atrasou. Diga ao Google em inglês: reconheça o marco perdido, dê o motivo em uma frase e aponte que você tem um plano de recuperação.
takeaways: I can say 'We missed the milestone' with calm.
I can give the reason in one short line.
I can take responsibility for a delay.
I can point to a recovery plan to Google.

teacher.overview: M4 — Coração do programa — negociação comercial com o Google em torno do data center. Cobre defesa de margem, mudança de escopo (change order), force majeure, contract clauses, BATNA, c…
teacher.focus: Números, valores, prazos e defesa de posição (tréplica).

flow.how: Aluno reconta em inglês, em 60s, o que praticou na aula anterior.
Frase-base fixa; troque um elemento por vez (cliente, prazo, valor), oralmente.
Negocie custo × prazo × escopo no contexto do cliente.
Grave 60s para o portfólio de fala do aluno.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Números são o calcanhar: drill em voz alta.
Insistir na 2ª e 3ª troca (tréplica).

practiceBank.title: Abrindo a conversa do marco perdido
practiceBank.how: Aluno é o gerente da Racional; professor é o Google. O marco de liberação do data hall não foi cumprido. Aluno abre de frente: reconhece ('to acknowledge'), dá o motivo curto ('the reason was') e mostra o 'recovery plan'. Tom firme e calmo. Professor pressiona um pouco.
lines: Set the role-play: 'You're the Racional manager; I'm Google. The data hall release milestone was missed. Open it head-on — acknowledge, give the short reason, show the recovery plan. Calm and firm.'
Start them: 'Begin with: I want to be straight with you — we missed the milestone.'
Pressure: 'How could this happen?'
Pressure: 'How do I know your recovery plan will hold?'
Require: 'Use to acknowledge, the reason was and recovery plan.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Do atraso ao plano de recuperação
practiceBank.how: Professor descreve por que o marco escorregou ('to slip') no data center. Aluno deve, oralmente, identificar a 'root cause', assumir responsabilidade ('to take responsibility') e propor como 'bring it back on track'. Professor questiona a viabilidade do plano.
lines: Set the scenario: 'I'll describe why the milestone slipped at the data center. Identify the root cause, take responsibility, and propose how to bring it back on track.'
Describe: 'The structure work fell behind because steel deliveries were late...'
Question viability: 'How realistic is that plan, really?'
Require: 'Use to slip, root cause, to take responsibility, to bring back on track.'

practiceBank.title: Mensagem honesta de 60 segundos
practiceBank.how: Aluno grava 60s comunicando ao Google que o marco foi perdido, usando 'to be straight with you', 'to take responsibility' e 'to make it right'. Deve soar honesto, não defensivo. Professor avalia tom e devolve correções.
lines: Dictate the task: 'Record 60 seconds telling Google the milestone was missed. Sound honest, not defensive.'
Require these words: 'to be straight with you', 'to take responsibility', 'to make it right'.
Start them: 'Open with: I want to be straight with you about the milestone.'
After listening, give tone feedback — where it sounded defensive vs firm.

practiceBank.title: Aluno vira o Google bravo
practiceBank.how: Aluno assume o papel do cliente Google insatisfeito com o marco perdido; professor responde como Racional. Depois trocam. O objetivo é o aluno sentir as duas pontas e praticar 'going forward', 'recovery plan', 'honest'.
lines: Flip roles: 'You're the angry Google client; I'm Racional. Then we swap.'
Prompt as coach: 'As the client, push hard on why the milestone was missed.'
After swap: 'Now you're Racional — answer with composure.'
Require: 'Use going forward, recovery plan and honest.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: De desculpa fraca a postura firme
practiceBank.how: Professor dá frases evasivas ('It wasn't our fault'). Aluno reformula para versões responsáveis e firmes ('We take responsibility, and here's the recovery plan'). Pratica 'to acknowledge', 'to take responsibility', 'to commit to'.
lines: Drill, I give an evasive line, you reshape it as responsible and firm: 'It wasn't our fault.' → 'We take responsibility, and here's the recovery plan.'
'The supplier let us down.' → 'I acknowledge the milestone slipped; we take responsibility and we're committing to a recovery plan.'
'These things happen.' → 'To be straight with you, we missed it — and here is how we'll make it right going forward.'

practiceBank.title: Reunião de acompanhamento difícil
practiceBank.how: Simulem a reunião completa: aluno reconhece o marco perdido, explica 'root cause', apresenta 'recovery plan' e fecha com 'going forward'. Professor faz 3 objeções. Aluno conduz a reunião até o acordo. Foco em manter o tom calmo.
lines: Open the simulation: 'Run the full meeting — acknowledge the missed milestone, explain the root cause, present the recovery plan, close with going forward. I'll raise three objections.'
Objection: 'Why should I trust this won't repeat?'
Objection: 'Your root cause sounds like an excuse.'
Objection: 'How firm is this recovery plan?'
Require: 'Keep the tone calm; use root cause, recovery plan, going forward.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Telefonema do marco perdido
practiceBank.how: Sentados de costas (sem vídeo), aluno liga para o Google avisando do marco perdido. Sem apoio visual, precisa estruturar: fato, motivo, plano. Usa 'to miss a milestone', 'the reason was', 'recovery plan'. Professor reage como cliente.
lines: Back-to-back call setup: 'No video. Call Google about the missed milestone — structure it: fact, reason, plan.'
Start them: 'Open with: I'm calling to be straight with you — we missed a milestone.'
React as client: 'Which milestone, and why?'
Require: 'Use to miss a milestone, the reason was and recovery plan.'

practiceBank.title: Qual motivo apresentar primeiro
practiceBank.how: Professor lista possíveis causas do atraso (chuva, fornecedor, mão de obra). Aluno ordena qual mencionar primeiro ao Google e justifica em inglês por que essa ordem é mais honesta e construtiva. Usa 'root cause', 'honest', 'to be straight with you'.
lines: Set the ranking: 'Here are possible causes of the delay — rain, supplier, labor. Rank which to mention first to Google and justify why that order is most honest and constructive.'
Prompt: 'Which cause do you lead with, and why?'
Push: 'Why not blame the rain first to soften it?'
Require: 'Use root cause, honest and to be straight with you.'

practiceBank.title: Um minuto assumindo responsabilidade
practiceBank.how: Aluno fala 60s sem parar assumindo a responsabilidade pelo marco perdido e detalhando como vai 'make it right'. Sem hesitar muito. Professor cronometra e marca onde o tom soou defensivo em vez de firme.
lines: Just a minute: 'Talk for 60 seconds, no stopping, taking responsibility for the missed milestone and how you'll make it right.'
Require: 'to take responsibility, to make it right, recovery plan, going forward.'
Start them: 'Begin with: I take full responsibility for this missed milestone.'
Note: 'Marco onde o tom soou defensivo em vez de firme.'

practiceBank.title: Professor empurra a culpa para fora
practiceBank.how: Professor insiste que o aluno culpe terceiros pelo marco perdido. Aluno resiste e mantém a postura de 'to take responsibility' e 'to be straight with you', sem jogar a culpa. Exercita firmeza diplomática sob pressão.
lines: Set the devil's advocate: 'I'll keep pushing you to blame others for the missed milestone. Resist — stay in responsibility.'
Push: 'Come on, the supplier caused this — just say it.'
Push: 'Nobody would blame you for pointing at the weather.'
Require: 'Hold the line with to take responsibility and to be straight with you.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Terminando a conversa difícil
practiceBank.how: Professor começa a fala ('I'm afraid we missed the milestone, and the reason was...'). Aluno completa oralmente até o plano de recuperação e o fechamento 'going forward'. Trocam quem começa. Foco em encadear as fases da conversa.
lines: Complete-the-story setup: 'I start the line, you finish it through to the recovery plan and the going forward close.'
Start: 'I'm afraid we missed the milestone, and the reason was...'
Prompt: 'Now you continue — root cause, plan, close.'
Swap: 'Now you start, I finish. Use to slip, recovery plan, going forward.'

practiceBank.title: Cadeira quente do data hall atrasado
practiceBank.how: Aluno na cadeira quente; professor dispara perguntas duras sobre o marco perdido do data hall ('Why did it slip?', 'How do I know it won't happen again?'). Aluno responde tudo na hora com 'to commit to', 'recovery plan', 'going forward'.
lines: Set the hot seat: 'You're on the hot seat for the late data hall. We fire hard questions — answer all on the spot.'
Ask: 'Why did it slip?'
Ask: 'How do I know it won't happen again?'
Ask: 'What exactly is your recovery plan?'
Require: 'Use to commit to, recovery plan and going forward.'
(Corrija só no final.)

leadIn: Have you ever had to tell Google a milestone was missed? How did you open it?
When a milestone slips, what's the first thing you should do — explain or acknowledge?
Why does taking responsibility build more trust than blaming the supplier?
What goes into a good recovery plan to bring a project back on track?
What does 'being straight with the client' mean to you?

pill.tip: Para soar educado, use "could you" (cud iú) com entonação suave, sem cair como uma ordem reta. Um leve toque ascendente no fim transmite cortesia.
pill.sample: Could you share the deck before noon?

lessons.title: Backup systems — diesel generators, fuel storage
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao Google, de forma simples, como o sistema de backup do data center funciona — geradores a diesel e estoque de combustível que mantêm a energia se a rede falhar. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
A data center must never lose power. Servers run all day and all night. If the grid power fails, the building needs a backup system. This is one of the most important parts of a Google data center.

The backup system uses diesel generators. When grid power fails, the generators switch on automatically. They keep the data center online at full load. To run for many hours, the site has large fuel storage tanks. The system must be reliable every single time.

Racional builds this kind of complex infrastructure. In data center work for clients like Google, power backup is critical. The Racional team installs the generators, the tanks, and the controls. A simple, clear explanation in English helps the client trust the work.
lessons.intro:
O tema é técnico, mas as frases são curtas. Foque em: "The backup system uses diesel generators." e "The generators switch on automatically."

Use também "if grid power fails" (se a rede falhar) e "fuel storage tanks" (tanques de combustível) para explicar a autonomia.
lessons.situation: Visita técnica com a equipe do Google ao data center. Eles perguntam o que acontece se a energia da rede cair. Você explica o sistema de backup em frases simples.
lessons.context: The data center needs power all the time. If grid power fails, our backup system starts. We use diesel generators. They switch on automatically and keep the site at full load. We have large fuel storage tanks for many hours.

vocab.example: If the grid power fails, the backup starts.
We keep the data center online.
We are ready for a power outage.
We refuel the tanks every week.

exercises.title: 1. Termo técnico e tradução
exercises.explanation: Quatro termos-chave do backup de energia: o que mantém o data center vivo.

exercises.title: 2. Explique o backup ao Google
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases explicando, de forma simples, o sistema de backup do data center. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: If grid power fails, our backup system starts. We use diesel generators, and they switch on automatically to keep the site at full load.
exercises.explanation: Causa (a rede falha) e solução (o backup liga). Frases curtas, ideia clara.

exercises.title: 3. Responda à pergunta do Google
exercises.prompt: O Google pergunta: 'What happens if grid power fails?'. Você responde:

options.text: Our diesel generators switch on automatically.
The data center stops and we wait.
options.whyWrong: O data center não pode parar. O backup deve manter tudo online.

options.text: We have no backup system here.
options.whyWrong: Um data center sempre tem backup. A resposta certa mostra os geradores.

exercises.title: 4. Monte a frase do backup
exercises.explanation: 'The generators switch on automatically.' — sujeito + verbo + advérbio. Direto.

exercises.title: 5. Explique em voz alta
exercises.targetText: If grid power fails, our diesel generators switch on automatically. We keep the data center online at full load.
exercises.translation: Se a energia da rede falhar, nossos geradores a diesel ligam automaticamente. Mantemos o data center funcionando em carga total.
exercises.prompt: Na visita técnica, explique ao Google o que acontece se a energia da rede cair.
exercises.explanation: Primeiro o cenário (a rede falha), depois a solução (os geradores ligam). Calmo e claro.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, imagine a visita técnica com o Google. Explique em inglês, em frases simples, o que acontece com a energia se a rede cair: os geradores a diesel ligam e mantêm o data center online.
takeaways: I can explain the backup system in simple words.
I can say 'The generators switch on automatically'.
I can talk about fuel storage and full load.
I can answer 'What happens if grid power fails?'.

Adivinhe um equipamento fazendo perguntas em inglês.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Pronúncia de termos técnicos.
Aluno deve explicar, não só reconhecer o termo.

practiceBank.title: Explicando o backup na visita técnica
practiceBank.how: Professor é a equipe do Google em visita ao data center e pergunta 'What happens if grid power fails?'. Aluno explica em frases simples: 'diesel generators switch on automatically', 'fuel storage keeps us online'. Professor pede mais detalhes a cada resposta.
lines: I'm the Google site team. Tell me: what happens if grid power fails?
And how fast do the diesel generators switch on?
You said 'automatically' — does anyone need to press a button?
Good. How long can the fuel storage keep us online?
When exactly do you refuel, and who decides? (Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Desenho do sistema de backup
practiceBank.how: Professor mostra (ou desenha) o esquema: grid → ATS → gerador diesel → tanque de combustível. Aluno descreve oralmente o fluxo usando 'backup system', 'grid power', 'to fail', 'to switch on', 'full load'. Professor aponta para partes aleatórias e pede a explicação.
lines: Aponte para o 'grid power' e peça: 'Start here. What is this and what happens when it fails?'
Aponte para o ATS: 'And this box — what does it do when the grid power fails?'
Aponte para o gerador: 'This unit — when does it switch on, and at what load?'
Aponte para o tanque: 'And this — what feeds the generator at full load?'
Aponte aleatório de novo e peça: 'Explain the whole flow from grid to generator in one go.'

practiceBank.title: E se a energia cair?
practiceBank.how: Professor faz perguntas curtas de cliente ('What if the grid fails?', 'How long can you run?', 'When do you refuel?'). Aluno responde cada uma em 1-2 frases com 'power outage', 'to keep online', 'to refuel', 'reliable'. Depois invertem os papéis.
lines: What if the grid fails right now?
How long can you run on a full tank?
When do you refuel?
How do you keep the data center online during a long power outage?
Why should the client call this system reliable?
(Agora invertam os papéis: o aluno faz as perguntas ao professor.)

practiceBank.title: Explicação do backup em 60 segundos
practiceBank.how: Aluno grava 60s explicando, para um cliente leigo do Google, como o backup mantém o data center funcionando. Tem que usar 'diesel generator', 'fuel storage', 'automatically', 'reliable'. Professor checa clareza e simplicidade.
lines: Start with: 'Let me explain how our backup keeps the data center online.'
Require these words: 'diesel generator', 'fuel storage', 'automatically', 'reliable'.
Keep it simple — imagine a non-technical Google client.
Follow-up: 'In one sentence, why is it reliable?'

practiceBank.title: Reconstruir o parágrafo do backup
practiceBank.how: Professor lê 2x um parágrafo curto sobre o funcionamento do backup (grid falha → geradores ligam → tanque alimenta). Aluno reconstrói oralmente o sentido com suas palavras, recuperando o vocab 'to fail', 'fuel', 'tank', 'full load'.
lines: Vou ler 2x este parágrafo: 'When grid power fails, the diesel generators switch on automatically. The fuel tank feeds them at full load and keeps the data center online until we refuel.'
Agora reconstrua o sentido com suas palavras, em voz alta.
Recupere obrigatoriamente: 'to fail', 'fuel', 'tank', 'full load'.
Follow-up: 'Now say only the technical steps, in order.'

practiceBank.title: Briefing técnico de resiliência
practiceBank.how: Aluno conduz um briefing para o Google sobre a estratégia de energia de backup do data center: o que acontece em 'power outage', tempo de autonomia, abastecimento. Professor faz papel de cliente técnico que questiona a confiabilidade ('reliable').
lines: I'm the Google technical client. Brief me on your backup energy strategy.
What exactly happens during a power outage?
How many hours of autonomy do you have at full load?
Convince me this is reliable — how do you guarantee refueling in time?
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Encaixar 8 termos na explicação
practiceBank.how: Professor entrega 8 cartões de vocab (generator, fuel storage, tank, automatically, etc.). Aluno explica o sistema de backup obrigatoriamente encaixando cada termo no momento certo, virando o cartão ao usá-lo. Professor confere uso correto.
lines: Entregue os 8 cartões: generator, fuel storage, tank, automatically, full load, to refuel, power outage, reliable.
Diga: 'Explain the backup system and use every card. Flip each card when you say the word.'
Se pular um termo, peça: 'You still have this card — fit it in.'
Follow-up: 'Now repeat the explanation without the cards.'

practiceBank.title: Tanque baixo durante apagão
practiceBank.how: Professor cria o cenário: apagão prolongado e tanque chegando a 30%. Aluno explica oralmente o plano: manter 'full load', 'to refuel' a tempo, manter o data center 'online'. Professor introduz complicações para o aluno reagir.
lines: Cenário: 'There is a long power outage and the fuel tank is down to 30%.' What is your plan?
Complicação: 'The fuel supplier says the truck is two hours away. Now what?'
Complicação: 'A second feeder also tripped. How do you keep full load?'
Require: 'full load', 'to refuel', 'to keep online'. (Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Dois sistemas de backup
practiceBank.how: Professor descreve dois diagramas de backup ligeiramente diferentes (um com 2 geradores, outro com 3; tanques de tamanhos diferentes). Aluno faz perguntas e aponta as diferenças em inglês, usando 'generator', 'tank', 'fuel storage', 'full load'.
lines: Descreva os dois sistemas: 'Diagram A has 2 generators and one big tank; Diagram B has 3 generators and two smaller tanks.'
Diga: 'Ask me questions and tell me the differences in English.'
Force o uso de: 'generator', 'tank', 'fuel storage', 'full load'.
Follow-up: 'Which design do you think is more reliable, and why?'

practiceBank.title: A noite em que a rede caiu
practiceBank.how: Aluno narra uma história: a 'grid power' caiu às 2h e o 'backup system' assumiu. Deve descrever passo a passo, usando 'to fail', 'to switch on', 'automatically', 'to keep online'. Professor escuta e depois pede que repita só a parte técnica.
lines: Start with: 'It was 2 a.m. when the grid power failed at the data center.'
Narre passo a passo: grid fails → generators switch on automatically → tank keeps us online.
Require: 'to fail', 'to switch on', 'automatically', 'to keep online'.
Follow-up: 'Now repeat only the technical part.'

practiceBank.title: PT → EN do sistema de backup

O tanque mantém a energia. → The fuel tank keeps us online.
Reabastecemos antes de acabar. → We refuel before it runs out.
Ritmo rápido — repita até automatizar 'automatically' e 'to refuel'.

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sobre confiabilidade
practiceBank.how: Aluno fala 60s sem parar sobre por que o backup do data center é 'reliable', cobrindo geradores, combustível e automação. Professor cronometra e marca pausas. Refazer buscando mais fluidez na 2ª tentativa.
lines: Diga: 'Speak for 60 seconds, non-stop, on why our backup is reliable.'
Cubra: generators, fuel, automation.
Cronometre e marque cada pausa.
2ª tentativa: 'Again — same minute, but smoother.'

pill.region: Evitar fillers — pausar em vez de 'uh'

lessons.title: Receiving feedback from Google politely
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você recebe feedback do Google de forma educada e profissional — mostra que escutou, concorda quando faz sentido e aponta o próximo passo. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
In every project, the client gives feedback. Google shares points to improve. Some feedback is easy to hear, and some is hard. The way you receive it says a lot about you and about Racional.

Good feedback skills are simple. You listen. You say "That's helpful" or "Good point". You show that you understand: "I see what you mean". Then you point to the next step: "We will look into it." You do not get defensive. You take the feedback on board and you act.

For Racional, listening well is part of strong client work. In over 620 projects, the best teams turn feedback into better results. With a client like Google, a calm and open answer keeps the relationship healthy and shows real professionalism.
lessons.intro:
Receber feedback bem é simples: escute, mostre que entendeu e aponte a ação.

Frases-âncora: "That's helpful.", "I see what you mean.", "Good point." e "We will look into it." Nunca fique na defensiva.
lessons.situation: Reunião de revisão com o Google. Eles dão feedback sobre um ponto do projeto que pode melhorar. Você escuta e responde de forma aberta e educada.
lessons.context: Thank you for the feedback. That's helpful. I see what you mean, and you are right. It is a good point. We will look into it and adjust the plan. I appreciate it.

vocab.pt: entendo o que você quer dizer

vocab.example: We will take it on board.

exercises.title: 1. Receba o feedback com classe
exercises.prompt: O Google aponta algo que pode melhorar. Você responde:

options.text: That's helpful. I see what you mean. We will look into it.
No, that is wrong. The plan is perfect.
options.whyWrong: Ficar na defensiva fecha a conversa. Mostre que escutou.

options.text: I do not have time for this now.
options.whyWrong: Frio e fechado. Receba o feedback e aponte uma ação.

exercises.title: 2. Resposta educada e tradução
exercises.explanation: Frases curtas que mostram escuta e abertura ao Google.

exercises.title: 3. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: Thank you for the feedback. We will look into it.
exercises.explanation: Agradeça o feedback e aponte a ação. Educado e profissional.

exercises.title: 4. Responda ao feedback do Google
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases respondendo, de forma educada, a um feedback do Google. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: Thank you for the feedback. That's a good point, and you are right. We will look into it and adjust the plan. I appreciate it.
exercises.explanation: Escuta + concordância + ação. É o jeito profissional de receber feedback.

exercises.title: 5. Responda em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Thank you for the feedback. I see what you mean. We will look into it and adjust the plan.

exercises.explanation: Agradeça, mostre que entendeu e aponte a ação. Tom calmo e aberto.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, imagine que o Google deu um feedback sobre o projeto. Responda em inglês de forma educada: agradeça, mostre que entendeu e diga que vai analisar e ajustar.
takeaways: I can receive feedback in a polite way.
I can say 'I see what you mean' and 'good point'.
I can say 'We will look into it'.
I can thank Google with 'I appreciate it'.

practiceBank.how: Primeiro o aluno é o Google dando feedback ao professor; depois recebem trocados. Ao receber, o aluno pratica 'that's helpful', 'fair enough', 'I appreciate it', 'noted'. Foco em soar aberto e não defensivo nas duas pontas.
